It's so simple that any name is an overdetermination. It's so accepting that any name will fit. It's so great that no name could contain it. It's so complex that no name could pretend to represent its fathoming. But name or no name, I know it inside and out, as it has nothing to hide, and truer still, I am dumbfounded, utterly stilted by awe, because it offers nothing to see. And yet I see it everywhere, for verily it is this seeing. And I am known by it, and this companionship is my power, my passion and my joy, many in effect, singular in identity.
